intro: Welcome back! In the last lesson you imagined a different past with if: If I had known, I would have come. Today you'll say what you wish were different, now and in the past (I wish I could speak Japanese, I wish I had studied harder), what you or others should have done, and how to say politely what you'd prefer: I'd rather stay home, It's time we went home.
teachingNotes: Recap in one line, don't re-teach: from b1-second-conditional the learner knows that a past form can mean 'not real now' (If I had more time = I don't have more time; were for every person), and from b2-third-conditional that the past perfect means 'not real in the past' (If I had known = I didn't know), plus would / could / might have + third form. New idea, the same 'one step back': after wish / if only the verb moves back from reality. Wish about NOW -> past simple (I wish I had a car, I wish I lived closer, I wish I could swim, I wish I were / was taller); wish about the PAST -> past perfect (I wish I had studied harder, I wish I hadn't said that). If only = the same patterns, stronger and more emotional. Indonesian 'andai saja / seandainya / coba' map to wish / if only; the Indonesian verb doesn't change, the English verb does.

wish + would: for other people's behaviour or things you want to change (often annoyance, or a change you hope for): I wish you would stop interrupting me, I wish it would stop raining. Not with I: *'I wish I would ...' -> I wish I could ... / I wish I + past simple (you control your own actions). Common errors and why: *'I wish I can speak Japanese' -> I wish I could (one step back: can -> could). *'I wish I would have more time' -> I wish I had more time. *'I wish I studied harder last year' -> I wish I had studied (past -> past perfect). *'He wish' -> he wishes. Trap: wish vs hope. Indonesian 'semoga' = hope, for real possibilities: I hope you pass the exam, NOT 'I wish you pass'. Name the other wish patterns so they don't look like broken rules: wish + person + noun (I wish you luck, We wish you a happy Eid) and formal wish to (= want: I wish to make a complaint). were / was after I wish: both correct, were is more formal; accept both.

should have / shouldn't have + third form (objective should-have): regret about your own past (I should have left earlier = harusnya tadi saya berangkat lebih awal, but I didn't) and criticism of someone else's past action (You shouldn't have shouted at him = seharusnya kamu tidak membentaknya, but you did). Recap: should + base verb (b1) is advice now or for the future; for the past English adds have + third form. Indonesian 'harusnya kemarin ...' keeps the same verb, so learners write *'You shouldn't came late' -> You shouldn't have come late, or *'I should leave earlier yesterday' -> I should have left. In speech: should've ('SHUD-ev'), shouldn't have ('SHUD-nt-ev'); never write 'should of'. Link to the third conditional: I should have left earlier = If I had left earlier, I wouldn't have been late. Don't teach should have for expectations (They should have arrived by now) or must have / can't have / could have for deduction: those are other lessons.

would rather (objective would-rather-its-time): about yourself -> would rather / 'd rather + base verb, no to (I'd rather stay home, I'd rather not talk about it, I'd rather walk than take an ojek; Would you rather ...?). About another person -> would rather + person + past simple, meaning now or the future (I'd rather you didn't smoke here = please don't). 'd here is always would. Common errors: *'I'd rather to stay', *'I'd rather you don't smoke' (heard in casual speech, especially American, but the past is the standard form: teach and test the past, give partial credit for the present). Only test cases where it's clear whether the sentence is about the speaker or someone else.

it's time (objective would-rather-its-time): it's time + to + verb for a general 'now is the moment' (It's time to go), it's time for + noun (It's time for lunch), and it's time + person + past simple when something should already be happening, often with a little criticism or urgency (It's time we went home, It's high time you found a new job; high / about = stronger, it's late already). Common error: *'It's time we go home' -> It's time we went home (one step back again). Indonesian 'sudah waktunya kita pulang' has no tense, so learners keep the present. Limits: no as if / as though, no 'had better', no inversion (Had I known), no wish + could have. If asked, say they come later. B2 contexts: office, startup, campus, KRL / MRT, ojek online, Lebaran tickets, Jakarta, Bandung, Surabaya, rupiah.

keyPoints.title: wish / if only: one step back
keyPoints.explanation: To say you want something to be different, use wish or if only (stronger) and move the verb one step back from reality. About now: past simple (I wish I lived closer, I wish I could swim, I wish I were / was taller). About the past: past perfect (I wish I had studied harder). For other people's behaviour or things you want to change: would (I wish you would stop interrupting me). Not 'I wish I can' or 'I wish I would'. For real hopes, use hope, not wish: I hope you pass.

examples.en: I wish I could speak Japanese.
examples.id: Andai saja saya bisa bahasa Jepang.

examples.en: If only I had saved more money last year!
examples.id: Andai saja tahun lalu saya menabung lebih banyak!

examples.en: I wish you would stop checking your phone in meetings.
examples.id: Saya harap kamu berhenti main HP waktu rapat.

id.title: wish / if only: mundur satu langkah
id.explanation: Untuk bilang kamu ingin sesuatu berbeda, pakai wish atau if only (lebih kuat) dan mundurkan kata kerjanya satu langkah dari kenyataan. Tentang sekarang: past simple (I wish I lived closer, I wish I could swim, I wish I were / was taller). Tentang masa lalu: past perfect (I wish I had studied harder). Untuk kebiasaan orang lain atau hal yang ingin kamu ubah: would (I wish you would stop interrupting me). Bukan 'I wish I can' atau 'I wish I would'. Untuk harapan yang nyata (semoga), pakai hope, bukan wish: I hope you pass.

keyPoints.title: should have / shouldn't have + third form
keyPoints.explanation: For a regret or a criticism about the past, use should have + third form (it was a good idea, but it didn't happen) or shouldn't have + third form (it was a bad idea, but it happened). I should have left earlier. You shouldn't have come late. Not 'shouldn't came': after have, use the third form. In speech: should've ('SHUD-ev'); never write 'should of'.

examples.en: I should have left the office earlier.
examples.id: Harusnya tadi saya pulang dari kantor lebih awal.

examples.en: You shouldn't have shouted at the waiter.
We should have checked the address before we ordered the ojek.
examples.id: Harusnya kita cek alamatnya dulu sebelum pesan ojek.

id.title: should have / shouldn't have + bentuk ketiga
id.explanation: Untuk penyesalan atau kritik tentang masa lalu, pakai should have + bentuk ketiga (itu ide yang baik, tapi tidak terjadi) atau shouldn't have + bentuk ketiga (itu ide yang buruk, tapi terjadi). I should have left earlier. You shouldn't have come late. Bukan 'shouldn't came': setelah have, pakai bentuk ketiga. Saat bicara: should've ('SHUD-ev'); jangan pernah menulis 'should of'.

keyPoints.title: would rather and it's time
keyPoints.explanation: About yourself: would rather ('d rather) + base verb, no to: I'd rather stay home. About another person: would rather + person + past simple (meaning now or later): I'd rather you didn't smoke here. it's time + to + verb: It's time to go. it's time + person + past simple when it should already be happening: It's time we went home (not 'It's time we go'). It's high time = stronger, it's late already.

examples.en: I'd rather walk than take an ojek.
examples.id: Mendingan saya jalan kaki daripada naik ojek.

examples.en: I'd rather you didn't tell anyone about this.
examples.id: Saya lebih suka kamu tidak menceritakan ini ke siapa pun.

examples.en: It's high time you found a new job.
examples.id: Sudah saatnya (dari dulu) kamu cari pekerjaan baru.

id.title: would rather dan it's time
id.explanation: Tentang dirimu sendiri: would rather ('d rather) + kata kerja dasar, tanpa to: I'd rather stay home. Tentang orang lain: would rather + orang + past simple (artinya sekarang atau nanti): I'd rather you didn't smoke here. it's time + to + kata kerja: It's time to go. it's time + orang + past simple kalau sesuatu seharusnya sudah terjadi: It's time we went home (bukan 'It's time we go'). It's high time = lebih kuat, sudah terlambat.

guidedPractice.prompt: Sari is 155 cm tall and she wants to be a flight attendant, but the airline needs people who are 160 cm or taller. Complete with the verb in brackets: I wish I ___ (be) taller.
guidedPractice.hint: A wish about now: one step back to the past. For be, use were (or was in everyday speech).

guidedPractice.prompt: Correct the mistake: I wish I would have more free time at the weekend.
expected: i wish i had more free time at the weekend
i wish i had more free time on the weekend
guidedPractice.hint: A wish about your own life now: wish + past simple (have → had). Don't use would with I.

guidedPractice.prompt: Dimas's laptop crashed this morning and he lost two hours of work because he didn't save the file. Complete with should and the verb in brackets: I ___ (save) the file.
guidedPractice.hint: A regret about the past: should have + third form (save → saved).

guidedPractice.prompt: Your friend asks: 'Shall we eat out tonight?' You're tired and want to stay in. Complete with the verb in brackets: I'd rather ___ (cook) at home tonight.
guidedPractice.hint: would rather about yourself: + base verb, with no to.

guidedPractice.prompt: It's 7:30 and your office starts at 8:00. Complete with the verb in brackets: It's time ___ (leave) for work.
guidedPractice.hint: it's time + to + verb when there's no person after time.

independentPractice.prompt: Write two sentences with I wish: one about your life now and one about something in the past you would like to change.
expected: i wish i lived closer to my office i wish i had studied english earlier
i wish i could play the guitar i wish i hadn't sold my motorbike
i wish i had more free time i wish i had saved more money last year
independentPractice.hint: Now → I wish + past simple (or could). Past → I wish + had + third form.

expected: i should have gone to bed earlier
i shouldn't have spent so much money online
i should have answered my mother's call
i shouldn't have stayed up so late on sunday
independentPractice.hint: should have / shouldn't have + third form.

independentPractice.prompt: Your flatmate wants to play loud music late at night, and something else in your life needs to change soon. Write one sentence with I'd rather you … and one with It's time ….

i'd rather you turned the music down it's high time we cleaned the kitchen
independentPractice.hint: I'd rather you + past simple. It's time + person + past simple (or It's time to + verb).

assessment.prompt: Budi takes an ojek to work every day because he never learned to drive. Correct the mistake in what he says: I wish I can drive a car.
acceptableAnswers: i wish i could drive a car
if only i could drive a car
i wish i could drive
i wish i knew how to drive a car
i wish i was able to drive a car
i wish i were able to drive a car
i wish that i could drive a car
assessment.rubric: Correct: I wish I could drive a car (a wish about now: one step back, can → could). 'I wish I knew how to drive' is also correct. 'I wish I would drive a car' = 30 (no would with I). 'I wish I could drove' = 50. 'I hope I can drive a car' = 20 (that's a real hope, not a wish about now). Keeping 'I wish I can' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Last year Dimas turned down a job offer from a startup in Singapore. Now the startup is very successful. Complete what he says with the verb in brackets: 'I wish I ___ (accept) that offer.'
acceptableAnswers: had accepted
'd accepted
i wish i had accepted that offer
i wish i'd accepted that offer
assessment.rubric: Correct: had accepted / 'd accepted (a regret about the past: wish + past perfect). 'accepted' = 30 (past simple after wish is about now, but the offer was last year). 'would have accepted' = 20. 'had accept' = 60 (accept → accepted).

assessment.prompt: It has been raining all afternoon, and you want to go home from the office. Translate into English with wish (or if only) and would: Andai saja hujannya berhenti.
acceptableAnswers: i wish it would stop raining
i wish the rain would stop
if only it would stop raining
if only the rain would stop
i wish it'd stop raining
i wish it would stop raining now
i wish the rain would stop now
if only it would stop raining now
i wish that it would stop raining
i wish that the rain would stop
assessment.rubric: Correct: I wish / If only it would stop raining (or the rain would stop): wish + would for a change you want in something you can't control. 'I wish it stopped raining' = 60 (grammatical, but would is the natural choice for a change you're waiting for). 'I wish it will stop raining' = 30. 'I hope it stops raining' = 50 (natural, but the item asks for wish and would).

assessment.prompt: Yesterday a new employee left the office at 3 p.m. without telling anyone. Today Pak Hasan says to him: You shouldn't went home without telling me. Correct the mistake.
acceptableAnswers: you shouldn't have gone home without telling me
you should not have gone home without telling me
you shouldn't've gone home without telling me
assessment.rubric: Correct: You shouldn't have gone home without telling me (criticism of a past action: shouldn't have + third form; go → went → gone). 'shouldn't have went' = 60 (the third form of go is gone). 'shouldn't go home' = 40 (that's advice about now or the future, not yesterday). Keeping 'shouldn't went' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Budi wanted to go home to Surabaya for Lebaran, but when he tried to buy train tickets yesterday, they were all sold out. Complete what he says with should and the verb in brackets: 'I ___ (book) the tickets earlier.'
acceptableAnswers: should have booked
should've booked
i should have booked the tickets earlier
i should've booked the tickets earlier
assessment.rubric: Correct: should have booked / should've booked (a regret about the past: should have + third form). 'should book' = 30 (that's advice for now or the future). 'should have book' = 60. 'should booked' = 30. 'should of booked' = 50 (a spelling mistake for should've).

assessment.prompt: Bu Ani's son wants to drive to Bandung tonight, but there's heavy rain and she's worried. She says: 'I'd rather you ___ (not / drive) tonight.' Complete with the verb in brackets.
acceptableAnswers: didn't drive
did not drive
i'd rather you didn't drive tonight
i would rather you didn't drive tonight
i would rather you did not drive tonight
assessment.rubric: Correct: didn't drive (would rather + another person + past simple, for now or the future). 'don't drive' = 60 (heard in casual speech, but the standard form is the past). 'not drive' = 40 (that's the pattern for yourself: I'd rather not drive). 'wouldn't drive' = 30. 'to not drive' = 10.

assessment.prompt: It's 11 p.m. on Sunday, and Rina's younger brother is still watching TV, although he has an exam at 8 a.m. tomorrow. Correct the mistake in what she says: It's time you go to bed.
acceptableAnswers: it's time you went to bed
it is time you went to bed
it's high time you went to bed
it's about time you went to bed
it's time for you to go to bed
it is time for you to go to bed
assessment.rubric: Correct: It's time you went to bed (it's time + person + past simple: one step back, even though it's about now). It's time for you to go to bed is also correct. 'It's time you going to bed' = 20. 'It's time you would go to bed' = 30. 'It's time to go to bed' = 70 (correct English, but it drops 'you'). Keeping 'you go' = 0.

material.title: Wishes about now: one step back

blocks.text:
**Quick recap:** in the second conditional, a past form means **not real now**: *If I had a car* = I don't have a car. In the third conditional, the past perfect means **not real in the past**: *If I had known* = I didn't know.

**wish** works the same way. When you want your life **now** to be different, put the verb **one step back**, into the past:
- **wish + past simple**: *I wish I **lived** closer to my office.* (I don't.)
- **can → could**: *I wish I **could** swim.* (I can't.)
- **be → were / was**: *I wish I **were** taller.* (I'm not.)
- negative: *I wish I **didn't have** to work on Saturdays.* (I do.)

**If only** means the same, but it's **stronger**, more emotional, and often ends with **!**: *If only I had more time!*
With *he / she*, it's **wishes**: *Rina wishes she had a car.*

id.text:
**Ulasan singkat:** di second conditional, bentuk past berarti **tidak nyata sekarang**: *If I had a car* = saya tidak punya mobil. Di third conditional, past perfect berarti **tidak nyata di masa lalu**: *If I had known* = waktu itu saya tidak tahu.

**wish** bekerja dengan cara yang sama. Kalau kamu ingin hidupmu **sekarang** berbeda, mundurkan kata kerjanya **satu langkah**, ke bentuk past:
- **wish + past simple**: *I wish I **lived** closer to my office.* (kenyataannya tidak.)
- **can → could**: *I wish I **could** swim.* (kenyataannya tidak bisa.)
- **be → were / was**: *I wish I **were** taller.* (kenyataannya tidak.)
- negatif: *I wish I **didn't have** to work on Saturdays.* (kenyataannya harus.)

**If only** artinya sama, tapi **lebih kuat**, lebih emosional, dan sering diakhiri **!**: *If only I had more time!*
Dengan *he / she*, jadi **wishes**: *Rina wishes she had a car.*

blocks.text:
**Why the past, when it's about now?** It looks like a broken rule, but the past form here doesn't mean yesterday: it shows the situation is **far from reality** (*jauh dari kenyataan*), exactly as after *if* in the second conditional.
**were or was?** *I wish I were taller* is more formal; *I wish I was taller* is very common in speech. Both are correct.
**The Indonesian trap:** *Andai saja saya bisa bahasa Jepang* has no tense, so learners say 'I wish I **can** speak Japanese' ✗. English moves the verb back: **I wish I could speak Japanese** ✓.

id.text:
**Kenapa past, padahal tentang sekarang?** Kelihatannya melanggar aturan, tapi bentuk past di sini bukan berarti kemarin: bentuk ini menunjukkan situasinya **jauh dari kenyataan**, persis seperti setelah *if* di second conditional.
**were atau was?** *I wish I were taller* lebih formal; *I wish I was taller* sangat umum dalam percakapan. Keduanya benar.
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *Andai saja saya bisa bahasa Jepang* tidak punya tense, jadi pelajar bilang 'I wish I **can** speak Japanese' ✗. Bahasa Inggris memundurkan kata kerjanya: **I wish I could speak Japanese** ✓.

rows.en: I wish I had a car.
rows.note: now: I don't have a car

id.note: sekarang: kenyataannya saya tidak punya mobil

rows.en: Budi wishes he could work from home.
rows.id: Budi berharap dia bisa kerja dari rumah (tapi tidak bisa).

rows.en: I wish my office weren't so far from the MRT station.
rows.id: Andai saja kantor saya tidak sejauh itu dari stasiun MRT.

rows.en: If only I knew her phone number!
rows.id: Andai saja saya tahu nomor HP-nya!

id.note: if only = lebih kuat daripada wish

blocks.text:
**wish or hope?** Indonesian *semoga* is **hope**, for things that can really happen: **I hope you pass the exam** ✓ (not 'I wish you pass'). **wish** is for things that are **not** true or not likely: *I wish I were 20 again.*
**Other jobs of wish (not this pattern):** *I wish you luck. We wish you a happy Eid.* (wish + person + a good thing = *mendoakan*), and formal *I wish to make a complaint* (= I want to). These are fixed phrases, so they don't break the rule.

id.text:
**wish atau hope?** *Semoga* dalam bahasa Indonesia adalah **hope**, untuk hal yang benar-benar bisa terjadi: **I hope you pass the exam** ✓ (bukan 'I wish you pass'). **wish** untuk hal yang **tidak** benar atau kecil kemungkinannya: *I wish I were 20 again.*
**Tugas lain wish (bukan pola ini):** *I wish you luck. We wish you a happy Eid.* (wish + orang + hal baik = *mendoakan*), dan bentuk formal *I wish to make a complaint* (= I want to). Ini frasa tetap, jadi tidak melanggar aturan.

blocks.prompt: Dimas can't swim, and his friends are going snorkelling in Bali. He says: 'I wish I ___ swim.'
blocks.explain: A wish about **now**: the verb goes one step back, so *can* becomes **could**. *can* and *will* don't step back.

id.prompt: Dimas tidak bisa berenang, dan teman-temannya mau snorkeling di Bali. Lengkapi ucapannya: 'I wish I ___ swim.'
id.explain: Harapan tentang **sekarang**: kata kerjanya mundur satu langkah, jadi *can* menjadi **could**. *can* dan *will* tidak mundur.

id.title: Harapan tentang sekarang: mundur satu langkah

material.title: Regrets about the past, and wish + would

blocks.text:
**About the past:** when you regret something that already happened, go **one more step back**, to the **past perfect** (*had + third form*), just like the if-part of the third conditional:
- *I wish I **had studied** harder at university.* (I didn't.)
- *I wish I **hadn't said** that to my boss.* (I did.)
- *If only we **had left** earlier!* (We didn't.)

Look at the time words: *now, today, these days* → **past simple**; *yesterday, last year, at university, when I was young* → **past perfect**.

**wish + would:** when you want **someone else** (or something you can't control) to change, use **would + base verb**. It often sounds annoyed or impatient:
- *I wish you **would stop** interrupting me.*
- *I wish my neighbours **wouldn't park** in front of my gate.*
- *I wish the bus **would come**!*

id.text:
**Tentang masa lalu:** kalau kamu menyesali sesuatu yang sudah terjadi, mundur **satu langkah lagi**, ke **past perfect** (*had + bentuk ketiga*), sama seperti bagian if di third conditional:
- *I wish I **had studied** harder at university.* (kenyataannya tidak.)
- *I wish I **hadn't said** that to my boss.* (kenyataannya saya mengatakannya.)
- *If only we **had left** earlier!* (kenyataannya tidak.)

Perhatikan kata waktunya: *now, today, these days* → **past simple**; *yesterday, last year, at university, when I was young* → **past perfect**.

**wish + would:** kalau kamu ingin **orang lain** (atau sesuatu yang tidak bisa kamu kendalikan) berubah, pakai **would + kata kerja dasar**. Sering terdengar kesal atau tidak sabar:
- *I wish you **would stop** interrupting me.*
- *I wish my neighbours **wouldn't park** in front of my gate.*
- *I wish the bus **would come**!*

blocks.text:
**Not 'I wish I would'.** You control your own actions, so you don't wish that **you** would do something: just do it! Say **I wish I could …** (I'm not able to) or **I wish I + past simple** (about now): 'I wish I would have more time' ✗ → **I wish I had more time** ✓.
**Don't stop at one step for the past:** 'I wish I studied harder last year' ✗ → **I wish I had studied harder last year** ✓.
Indonesian uses the same *andai saja* or *coba* for now and for the past (*Coba dulu saya belajar lebih giat*). English shows the time in the **verb**.

id.text:
**Bukan 'I wish I would'.** Tindakanmu sendiri ada di tanganmu, jadi kamu tidak berharap **kamu** akan melakukan sesuatu: lakukan saja! Katakan **I wish I could …** (saya tidak mampu) atau **I wish I + past simple** (tentang sekarang): 'I wish I would have more time' ✗ → **I wish I had more time** ✓.
**Untuk masa lalu, jangan berhenti di satu langkah:** 'I wish I studied harder last year' ✗ → **I wish I had studied harder last year** ✓.
Bahasa Indonesia memakai *andai saja* atau *coba* yang sama untuk sekarang dan masa lalu (*Coba dulu saya belajar lebih giat*). Bahasa Inggris menunjukkan waktunya lewat **kata kerja**.

blocks.prompt: Your colleague always interrupts you in meetings. Which sentence is correct?
options: I wish he doesn't interrupt me.
I wish he wouldn't interrupt me.
I wish he won't interrupt me.
blocks.explain: You want **someone else's** behaviour to change: **wish + would / wouldn't + base verb**. After *wish*, the present (*doesn't*) and *will* (*won't*) don't step back from reality.

id.prompt: Rekan kerjamu selalu memotong omonganmu waktu rapat. Kalimat mana yang benar?
id.explain: Kamu ingin kebiasaan **orang lain** berubah: **wish + would / wouldn't + kata kerja dasar**. Setelah *wish*, bentuk present (*doesn't*) dan *will* (*won't*) tidak mundur dari kenyataan.

id.title: Penyesalan tentang masa lalu, dan wish + would

blocks.text:
**Recap:** **should + base verb** gives advice for now or later: *You should leave early tomorrow.*

For the **past**, add **have + third form**:
- **should have + third form** = it was a good idea, but it **didn't** happen (*harusnya …, tapi tidak*): *I **should have left** earlier.* (I didn't, and I was late.)
- **shouldn't have + third form** = it was a bad idea, but it **did** happen (*seharusnya tidak …*): *You **shouldn't have shouted** at him.* (You did.)

About yourself, it's a **regret**. About someone else, it's a **criticism**: *You should have told me!*

It's close to a third conditional: *I should have left earlier* ≈ *If I had left earlier, I wouldn't have been late.*

id.text:
**Ulasan:** **should + kata kerja dasar** memberi saran untuk sekarang atau nanti: *You should leave early tomorrow.*

Untuk **masa lalu**, tambahkan **have + bentuk ketiga**:
- **should have + bentuk ketiga** = itu ide yang baik, tapi **tidak** terjadi (*harusnya …, tapi tidak*): *I **should have left** earlier.* (kenyataannya tidak, dan saya terlambat.)
- **shouldn't have + bentuk ketiga** = itu ide yang buruk, tapi **terjadi** (*seharusnya tidak …*): *You **shouldn't have shouted** at him.* (kenyataannya kamu membentaknya.)

Tentang dirimu sendiri, ini **penyesalan**. Tentang orang lain, ini **kritik**: *You should have told me!*

Ini mirip third conditional: *I should have left earlier* ≈ *If I had left earlier, I wouldn't have been late.*

blocks.text:
**The Indonesian trap:** *Harusnya kemarin kamu tidak datang terlambat* keeps the same verb for the past, so learners say 'You shouldn't **came** late' ✗ or 'You shouldn't **come** late yesterday' ✗. English needs **have + third form**: **You shouldn't have come late** ✓ (*come → came → **come***).
**Say it:** *should have* sounds like **should've** ('SHUD-ev'), and *shouldn't have* like 'SHUD-nt-ev'. Because of the sound, people sometimes write 'should of' ✗. Write **should have** or **should've** ✓.

id.text:
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *Harusnya kemarin kamu tidak datang terlambat* memakai kata kerja yang sama untuk masa lalu, jadi pelajar bilang 'You shouldn't **came** late' ✗ atau 'You shouldn't **come** late yesterday' ✗. Bahasa Inggris perlu **have + bentuk ketiga**: **You shouldn't have come late** ✓ (*come → came → **come***).
**Cara mengucapkan:** *should have* terdengar seperti **should've** ('SHUD-ev'), dan *shouldn't have* seperti 'SHUD-nt-ev'. Karena bunyinya, orang kadang menulis 'should of' ✗. Tulis **should have** atau **should've** ✓.

blocks.prompt: Rina didn't back up her laptop, and now all her photos are gone. Which sentence is a regret about the past?
options: I should back up my laptop.
I should have backed up my laptop.
I should have back up my laptop.
blocks.explain: A regret about the past: **should have + third form** (*back up → backed up*). *I should back up* is advice for now or later, and after *have* you need the third form, not the base verb.

id.prompt: Rina tidak mem-backup laptopnya, dan sekarang semua fotonya hilang. Kalimat mana yang merupakan penyesalan tentang masa lalu?
id.explain: Penyesalan tentang masa lalu: **should have + bentuk ketiga** (*back up → backed up*). *I should back up* adalah saran untuk sekarang atau nanti, dan setelah *have* kamu perlu bentuk ketiga, bukan kata kerja dasar.

blocks.text:
**would rather** ('d rather) = *lebih suka, mendingan*. First ask: **who** is it about?
- **About yourself** → **would rather + base verb** (no *to*): *I'd rather **stay** home tonight.* Negative: *I'd rather **not** talk about it.* With two choices: *I'd rather **walk** than **take** an ojek.* Question: *Would you rather …?*
- **About another person** → **would rather + person + past simple**, even though it's about now or later: *I'd rather you **didn't smoke** here.* (= please don't.) *I'd rather you **came** tomorrow.*

The **'d** in *I'd rather* is always **would**.

**it's time** has three patterns:
- **it's time to + verb**: *It's time **to go**.* (a general 'now')
- **it's time for + noun**: *It's time **for lunch**.*
- **it's time + person + past simple**: it should **already** be happening (a little criticism or urgency): *It's time we **went** home.* **It's high time / It's about time** = even stronger: *It's high time you **found** a new job.*

id.text:
**would rather** ('d rather) = *lebih suka, mendingan*. Pertama, tanya: ini tentang **siapa**?
- **Tentang dirimu sendiri** → **would rather + kata kerja dasar** (tanpa *to*): *I'd rather **stay** home tonight.* Negatif: *I'd rather **not** talk about it.* Dengan dua pilihan: *I'd rather **walk** than **take** an ojek.* Pertanyaan: *Would you rather …?*
- **Tentang orang lain** → **would rather + orang + past simple**, walaupun tentang sekarang atau nanti: *I'd rather you **didn't smoke** here.* (= tolong jangan.) *I'd rather you **came** tomorrow.*

**'d** di *I'd rather* selalu **would**.

**it's time** punya tiga pola:
- **it's time to + kata kerja**: *It's time **to go**.* ('sekarang' secara umum)
- **it's time for + kata benda**: *It's time **for lunch**.*
- **it's time + orang + past simple**: seharusnya **sudah** terjadi (ada sedikit kritik atau desakan): *It's time we **went** home.* **It's high time / It's about time** = lebih kuat lagi: *It's high time you **found** a new job.*

blocks.text:
**Why the past again?** *It's time we went home* and *I'd rather you didn't smoke* are about **now**, but the action isn't happening yet: it's still not real. So the verb takes **one step back**, like after *wish*.
**Traps:** 'It's time we **go** home' ✗ → **It's time we went home** ✓ (Indonesian *sudah waktunya kita pulang* has no tense). 'I'd rather **to** stay' ✗ → **I'd rather stay** ✓. You may hear 'I'd rather you **don't** …' in casual speech (especially American), but the past is the standard form: use it at work and in tests.

id.text:
**Kenapa past lagi?** *It's time we went home* dan *I'd rather you didn't smoke* tentang **sekarang**, tapi tindakannya belum terjadi: masih belum nyata. Jadi kata kerjanya **mundur satu langkah**, seperti setelah *wish*.
**Jebakan:** 'It's time we **go** home' ✗ → **It's time we went home** ✓ (*sudah waktunya kita pulang* dalam bahasa Indonesia tidak punya tense). 'I'd rather **to** stay' ✗ → **I'd rather stay** ✓. Kamu mungkin mendengar 'I'd rather you **don't** …' dalam percakapan santai (terutama bahasa Inggris Amerika), tapi bentuk past adalah bentuk standarnya: pakai itu di kantor dan saat tes.

id.intro: Selamat datang lagi! Di pelajaran sebelumnya kamu membayangkan masa lalu yang berbeda dengan if: If I had known, I would have come. Hari ini kamu akan mengungkapkan apa yang kamu harap berbeda, sekarang maupun di masa lalu (I wish I could speak Japanese, I wish I had studied harder), apa yang seharusnya kamu atau orang lain lakukan, dan cara bilang dengan sopan apa yang kamu lebih suka: I'd rather stay home, It's time we went home.

assessment.wr-1: Budi naik ojek ke kantor setiap hari karena dia tidak pernah belajar menyetir. Perbaiki kesalahan dalam ucapannya: I wish I can drive a car.
assessment.wr-2: Tahun lalu Dimas menolak tawaran kerja dari sebuah startup di Singapura. Sekarang startup itu sangat sukses. Lengkapi ucapannya dengan kata kerja dalam kurung: 'I wish I ___ (accept) that offer.'
assessment.wr-3: Sudah hujan sepanjang sore, dan kamu ingin pulang dari kantor. Terjemahkan ke dalam bahasa Inggris dengan wish (atau if only) dan would: Andai saja hujannya berhenti.
assessment.wr-4: Kemarin seorang karyawan baru pulang dari kantor jam 3 sore tanpa memberi tahu siapa pun. Hari ini Pak Hasan berkata kepadanya: You shouldn't went home without telling me. Perbaiki kesalahannya.
assessment.wr-5: Budi ingin mudik ke Surabaya untuk Lebaran, tapi waktu dia mencoba membeli tiket kereta kemarin, semuanya sudah habis. Lengkapi ucapannya dengan should dan kata kerja dalam kurung: 'I ___ (book) the tickets earlier.'
assessment.wr-6: Anak Bu Ani mau menyetir ke Bandung malam ini, tapi hujannya deras dan Bu Ani khawatir. Dia berkata: 'I'd rather you ___ (not / drive) tonight.' Lengkapi dengan kata kerja dalam kurung.
assessment.wr-7: Jam 11 malam hari Minggu, dan adik laki-laki Rina masih menonton TV, padahal besok jam 8 pagi dia ujian. Perbaiki kesalahan dalam ucapan Rina: It's time you go to bed.
